after.description: emit N context lines after each match (-A)

before.description: emit N context lines before each match (-B)

context.description: Return N lines around each match — this turns a grep into a focused window read. To pull a value's whole table, grep one of its values (or the parameter name) with context ~20-40, instead of reading the whole document. Both sides; -A/-B override a side (-C).

count.description: output only a count of matching lines per chunk, not the lines (-c)

file_type.description: restrict to a single file type (-t)

fixed.description: Match the pattern as literal characters, with no regex meaning (`|`, `.`, `*` match themselves). Usually leave this off — use it only to find text that itself contains regex symbols (-F).

glob.description: only files whose path matches this ripgrep -g glob, e.g. **/* (all) or *<name-fragment>*

line_number.description: Show each match's line number within the chunk — the position of the hit, so you can point at where a value sits or read a window around that line (-n).

max_count.description: stop after N matching lines per chunk (-m)

multiline.description: let the pattern span lines: `.` matches newlines, matched against the whole chunk (-U)

only_matching.description: print only the matched substring(s), one per line, not the whole line (-o)

path.description: Search only this document — the same path `glob`/`read`/`search` show (a trailing `#chunk` is ignored). Omit to search the whole base.

pattern.description: The text to find. It is a regex by default, so `A|B` matches A or B, `[0-9]+` matches digits, `.` matches any character; plain text also works as-is. For a value list, grep one value or the parameter name with `context` to pull its table window.
